Compares actual price movement to a random-walk null hypothesis over n periods using ATR-normalized range: RWI High = (High - Low(n periods ago)) / (ATR(n)*sqrt(n)), RWI Low = (High(n periods ago) - Low) / (ATR(n)*sqrt(n)). Interpretation: RWI High > 1.0 and RWI Low < 1.0 signals a statistically-significant uptrend; RWI Low > 1.0 and RWI High < 1.0 signals downtrend; both < 1.0 = random/noise (no tradeable trend). Common threshold 1.0-1.5, common period n=14.
notes: First Random Walk Index strategy in this repo -- distinct from VHF/ADX/Choppiness Index (already tested, all trend-strength-not-direction concepts) since RWI directly compares to a statistical random-walk null hypothesis rather than a raw range-vs-path ratio.

summary: DeMarker (DeM) indicator by Thomas DeMark: DeMax=max(high-high[1],0), DeMin=max(low[1]-low,0), DeM=SMA(DeMax,n)/(SMA(DeMax,n)+SMA(DeMin,n)) scaled 0-1 (or 0-100), default n=14. >0.7 overbought/exhaustion, <0.3 oversold/exhaustion; used for reversal/exhaustion signals, often combined with trend filter.

Full VIDYA (Tushar Chande, 1992) formula and rule disclosed free: VIDYA is an EMA-style adaptive average whose smoothing constant scales with abs(CMO)/100 (Chande Momentum Oscillator, typically 9-bar lookback) -- high abs(CMO)=fast-moving VIDYA (trending), low abs(CMO)=slow/flat VIDYA (ranging). Mechanical crossover rule: buy when price crosses above VIDYA while VIDYA is rising (slope>0); exit when price crosses below VIDYA while VIDYA is falling.
